title: Shot Studio — prompt composer notes
content: TL;DR: sketching a lightweight ‘Shot Studio’ — a composable prompt / example snippet library + visual composer for building production prompt bundles. Target: developer and ML engineer workflows that want reusable building blocks (instructions, shots, transformers) + preview run & cost/latency estimation before deploying into Redwood routes. MVP should focus on local composition, versioning, and Export-to-API flow (SDK/cli).
content_long:
Problem context:
- Teams re-create similar few-shot examples & instruction scaffolding across projects. Hard to reuse, audit, and iterate on prompts in a disciplined way.
- Onboarding new devs: copy-paste sprawl. No easy way to preview how combining components affects cost/latency/qualities.
- Current Console has route-level prompt editor but lacks modular primitives and team gallery.

Vision (one-liner):
A small studio for building, testing, and sharing composable prompt "shots" and prompt recipes — first-class artifacts that can be versioned, parameterized, and plugged into Redwood routes or SDK calls.

Core concepts / vocabulary:
- Shot: a reusable snippet (instruction, example, system message, regex filter, post-process cmd).
- Bundle / Recipe: ordered set of shots + metadata (placeholders, expected input/output schema).
- Variant: a forked version of a shot (for canary/AB testing).
- Binding: mapping between external data fields and placeholders in a bundle.
- Preview run: run a composed bundle against a controlled input with token/cost/latency estimate.

MVP feature list (priority):
1) Shot library (CRUD) — simple text + optional typed fields. Tagging, search, and quick-insert.
2) Composer canvas — drag-to-order shots, define placeholders, save as recipe.
3) Preview runner — run example inputs, show delta in tokens and latency vs baseline. Simple histogram of response length.
4) Export to SDK/Console route — one-click to attach recipe to a hosted route or produce SDK JSON that can be pasted.
5) Versioning + snapshot — each recipe save creates snapshot; can rollback.

Stretch / phase 2 ideas:
- Team gallery with access controls and popularity metrics.
- Canary variants and automatic A/B in Console.
- Param templates + runtime parameter validation.
- Marketplace for curated shots (internal OSS-esque).
- Quality hooks: tie a recipe to eval prompt sets and track regressions.

User stories:
- As an ML eng, I want to save a few-shot example as a named shot so I can reuse it across multiple routes without copy-paste.
- As a product dev, I want to preview how adding a long system instruction changes token usage so I can make tradeoffs.
- As an infra engineer, I want recipe exports to include metadata to enable consistent KV cache keys for prefix caching.
- As a team lead, I want to see who edited a shot and roll back to an earlier snapshot if a change caused regressions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create/Edit/Delete shots in library; shots are searchable by tag.
- Compose a recipe from at least 3 shot types (system+example+post-process) and save.
- Run preview: results include generated output, token count, estimated cost, and observed latency (on-hosted dev environment).
- Export: generate SDK snippet (javascript/python) that calls Redwood API with the composed bundle.

UX sketches / flows (notes to self):
- Left rail: library filter (type, tag, author). Middle canvas: ordered list with drag handles. Right rail: preview & metadata. Top: quick-save + 'export' + 'snapshot history' buttons.
- Quick insert: keyboard shortcut to insert last-used shot.
- Inline placeholders highlighted with blue pill UI; clicking opens binding modal to map to input fields or runtime params.

API/SDK shape (quick idea):
- POST /v1/recipes (body: {name, shots: [{id,type,content,placeholders}], metadata}) -> recipe_id
- GET /v1/recipes/:id/preview (query: input={...}) -> {tokens, est_cost, latency_ms, out}
- SDK helper: Redwood.shotCompose({recipeId, bindings, runtimeParams}) -> returns wire-format request to send to model endpoint.

Metrics to track (product + infra):
- Adoption: number of teams with >=1 recipe, active recipes per week.
- Reuse rate: percent of shots used in >1 recipe.
- Preview to export conversion rate.
- Average token delta caused by recipes (to estimate cost impact).

Privacy / security notes: 
- Shots may contain PII if users paste real examples. Default: mark all shots as plaintext, add 'redact-on-export' option, recommend using synthetic examples.
- Access controls: integrate with Console RBAC; default user-level visibility private.

Open questions / risks (todo):
- Canonical storage: store full text vs deduped refs? (dedupe helps disk and diffing but complexity for deletes)
- Cache interaction: how to compute safe cache keys for composed prefix? Need a deterministic canonicalization.
- Cost estimation accuracy: preview should use same tokenization as runtime; need offline tokenizer in Console.
- UX complexity: avoid creating a heavyweight builder — aim small, keyboard-first flows.
- Multi-model compatibility: recipes should declare model requirements (context window, recommended sampling). How strict?

Implementation notes / dev plan (rough):
Week 1-2: backend shot CRUD + simple DB schema (shots, recipes, snapshots).
Week 3: composer UI prototype + library rail.
Week 4: preview runner + token estimator service.
Week 5: export SDK generator + basic RBAC.
Week 6: internal alpha + feedback loop with 3 teams (GTM, Console, Solutions Eng).

Rollout & validation:
- Start with internal alpha; gather 10 recipe examples. Run small eval set to detect quality regressions when recipe is updated.
- Instrument telemetry: preview vs exported usage; collect developer feedback form inline.

Notes to self: 
- Talk to Maya about linking shot snapshots to our eval harness.
- Ask SRE about storing large public shot blobs — put limit of 32KB per shot for MVP.
- Consider 'minimap' UI for very long examples.

Todo list (next actions):
- [ ] Sketch composer mockups (Maya)
- [ ] Define DB schema draft (Kai)
footnote: This is a working draft. Lots of rough edges; intent is to get a narrow MVP that makes prompt reuse and previewing realistic for dev teams. Avoid scope creep (marketplace, paid tiers) in initial pass.
